environment: Existing Linux gate host; isolated disposable processes and scratch storage. Record host capacity, contention, OS, Java, ZooKeeper, disk, CPU, RAM and exact source checkout. Do not run alongside other builds or load tests.
head: 48a8565f384034202702c8cba37923fb3046c386
requirements: Before claiming, confirm host availability and resource budget and inspect existing Linux claims and running workloads; do not infer an idle host from a board release. If capacity or safe isolation is inadequate, report incomplete and stop.

Use a clean Apache Solr checkout at exactly 48a8565f384034202702c8cba37923fb3046c386 and record git status and full SHA. Use JDK 21 or version required by the pinned source; record actual version. Build the development distribution with ./gradlew dev on the Linux gate host and record command, exit code, and build log. No source edits.

Create a reproducible, documented client harness and isolated local SolrCloud topology: three Solr node processes and a separately managed ZooKeeper instance (or ensemble), fresh state for every run, fixed per-node heap/configuration. Make the actual launch and cleanup commands, configsets and scripts available with the evidence. Verify node health and actual coordination mode. Never touch existing host clusters or unrelated processes.

Primary comparison: collection CREATE with 1 shard and 2 replicas on independent names, empty identical configsets, 24 collections per run at client concurrency 1, 4 and 10. Use fresh cluster state for every run; 3 repetitions for each of 2 modes x 3 concurrency levels. If capacity cannot sustain 48 replicas, stop and report capacity and a revised proposed smaller topology; do not silently reduce. Alternate or randomize run order and record order. Warm up identically and exclude warmup from timed records.

Set overseerEnabled consistently before starting each disposable cluster and verify it for all nodes. Hold constant per-replica-state setting (explicitly record chosen value), node placement, receiver routing (one node for all requests), Solr and ZooKeeper versions, Java, heap, request counts, client retry policy, and timeouts. Do not perform a rolling mode switch.

Record a row per request with run id, exact source SHA, mode, concurrency, collection, receiver, submission time, terminal completion time and status, timeout/rejection/error and retry. An async request ID or HTTP acceptance is not completion. Use synchronous terminal responses or poll every async ID at a fixed equal cadence and report cadence. Count unfinished separately; never silently retry or drop errors. Verify expected shards/replicas are active, and capture per-run total completion time, successes, failures, timeouts and completed throughput.

Report median and p95 of terminal successful request latency, per-run rather than cherry-picked results, plus failure counts and throughput. With 24 samples per run label tail estimates as coarse. Retain raw CSV or JSONL, cluster logs, harness, configuration, commands, and host metrics (at least CPU, heap/GC and disk; ZooKeeper operations/latency if available; name exact metrics and collection method). Measure per-run changes as distributed vs Overseer and show repeat variability.

If safe capacity remains and the primary comparison completes, run an explicitly labeled optional second scenario: one receiver versus round-robin receivers at concurrency 10, keeping everything else constant. Do not report that optional leg as completed unless executed. Recovery, PRS variation, multi-host scalability and Mark Miller fork comparisons are out of scope and remain unmeasured.

Publish a receipt and report linking actual commands, artifact locations, full SHA, run-order, raw result summaries, environment and constraints. Results are descriptive evidence, not a pass/fail performance target; mark incomplete on setup failure, missing modes, unsuccessful runs, changed checkout or missing data, with actual failure details. No PR, Jira, mailing-list or other public communication is authorized by this job.
verdict_policy: passed means only that every mandatory measurement and evidence requirement ran successfully at the named head; it does not mean either mode won or prove production scalability.
